Arts Infliction.name: Arts Infliction
Arts Infliction.overview:
Arts Infliction is a debuff applied by both Operators and Enemies lasting for 20 seconds. If an Arts Infliction is applied to a unit who already has an Arts Infliction of the same element, then the debuff's duration is reset and the Arts Infliction gains a stack (up to a maximum of 4 stacks).

Friendly

Some Operators are capable of applying Arts Infliction.
* If an Operator applies an Arts Infliction to an enemy with Arts Infliction of the same element, then an Arts Burst is triggered dealing 160% ATK as Arts DMG based on the element.
* If an Operator applies an Arts Infliction to an enemy with Arts Infliction of a different element, then an Arts Reaction is triggered with the former determining the type of reaction and the latter determining the strength of the reaction.

Hostile

Some Enemies are capable of applying Heat Infliction and Cryo Infliction.

* If the Operator recieves 4 stacks of an Arts Infliction of the same element, then an Arts Reaction is triggered based on the element.

Arts Reaction.lead: Arts Reaction is a Combat Mechanic in Arknights: Endfield.
Arts Reaction.name: Arts Reaction
Arts Reaction.overview:
Arts Reactions are debuffs applied by both Operators and Enemies. The effects and duration of a debuff depends on its type and Status Level. 

Friendly

Some Operators are capable of applying Arts Reactions to Enemies.
* If an operator applies an Arts Infliction of one element to an enemy with Arts Infliction of a different element, then the first element is consumed to trigger an Arts Reaction.
** The first element may be referred to as the stacking element and determines the Status Level of the reaction.
** The second element may be referred to as the triggering element and determines the element of the reaction. The reaction also deals an initial instance of Arts DMG with the type based on this element and the damage amount based on the Status Level of the reaction.
* Some operator skills can also forcibly apply an Arts Reaction without requiring two different Arts Inflictions to be applied.
** Forced reactions do not consume any existing Arts Inflictions already applied on the enemy (if any) and apply the reaction as Status Level I (unless otherwise specified).
** Forced reactions do not deal the initial instance of Arts DMG caused by applying multiple Arts Inflictions of different elements.

Hostile

Some Enemies are capable of applying Arts Reactions.
* When an Operator reaches four stacks of Arts Inflictions of the same element, all existing Arts Infliction stacks of that element are removed to trigger an Arts Reaction.

* Strength (STR) influences the Operator's Max HP.

* Agility (AGL) influences the Operator's Physical DMG Reduction.

* Intellect (INT) influences the Operator's Arts DMG Reduction.

sections.Main Stats:
===HP===
HP, Max HP, Health or Health Points represent how much damage an Operator can take. It is visible on the Operator screen and on the blue HP bar. If an Operator reaches 0 HP they will become disconnected and won't be able to participate in combat anymore. A disconnected Operator can be resuscitated or revived using consumable items like Arts Tube or by resting at a TP Point.

All Operators have 500 Base HP at level 1 which linearly increases to 5495 Base HP at level 90. Additionaly each point of Strength increases the Base HP by 5. An Operator's Max HP can be further increased by certain Gear and Weapon effects. All sources of percentage increases to Max HP stack additively.
Some effects scale with the Max HP of an Operator. For example Ember's Ultimate and the ability of Thunderberge.

===Attack===
Unless otherwise noted, this is the base value for calculating almost all outgoing damage, and can be seen on the Operator sceen.

 FORMULA: Attack = ((Operator Attack + Weapon Attack) * Percentage Bonuses + Flat Increases ) * Attribute Bonuses

===Defense===
Defense, or DEF for short, gives an Operator Final DMG Reduction. All Operators have 0 and all enemies have 100 initial Defense, independent of their level. Defense is mainly increased by equipping Gear, and is otherwise only rarely increased by other sources. Catcher's Potential Bonus Spec Training for example grants him another 20 Defense.

 FORMULA: Defense Multiplier = cases (100)/(DEF + 100), & if DEF is 0 \\ 2-0.99^-DEF, & if DEF is < 0 cases

For example, equipping four pieces of Gear of the highest rarity gives 140 DEF, resulting in a 0.416 multiplier for incoming Damage, or 58.33% Final DMG Reduction.

sections.Actions:
===Dash/Dodge===
Dashes can be used to dodge enemy attacks. Dodging does not interrupt the basic attack sequence. A dodge performed at the moment of enemy attack triggers a Perfect Dodge that recovers some SP.

Dashes consume Stamina. The player will recover Stamina over time up to a cap. Players start with 3 sections of Stamina, submitting Aurylene of Valley IV at TP Points can raise the cap via Stamina Delimiter.

===Lock On===
Targets can be locked-on, which keeps the target in view and will make Skills used focus the target.

===Basic Attack===
Basic Attack Sequences can be performed by repeatedly pressing or long-pressing the attack button.

===Final Strike===
The last basic attack sequence is called the Final Strike. This move involves a short charge up followed by a powerful hit. The controlled Operator's Final Strike also deals Stagger and restores some Skill Points (SP).

===Finisher===
The first basic attack dealt to a Staggered enemy will be a Finisher that deals massive damage and restores some Skill Points (SP).

===Battle Skill===
The player can choose spend Skill Points to cast Operators' battle skills. Battle skills have no cooldown, and can be cast whenever there is enough SP and the respective Operator is not under a special status, such as knocked backed by an enemy attack.

===Combo Skill===
Operators' Combo Skills can be cast when certain criteria are met. Every Combo Skill has different triggers. Succesfully triggering a Combo Skill condition will make it appear on the screen, making it possible to cast it.

Combo Skills do not cost any Skill Points to cast. However, Combo Skills have cooldowns and cannot be triggered until the cooldown timer ends.

===Ultimate===
Operators with max Ultimate Energy can cast their Ultimates. There are 2 main ways to gain Ultimate Energy: Casting Battle Skills grant every teammate an equal amount of Ultimate Energy; casting Combo Skills grant only the caster Ultimate Energy. Though there are exceptions like Last Rite which do not gain Ultimate Energy from Battle Skills casted by other Operators. Casting the Ultimate will spend all Ultimate Energy and the Ultimate will enter a short cooldown. Some Operators' Ultimates enhance themselves. While their ultimate enhancement is active, no Ultimate Energy will be gained as well.

===Team Combat===
Other operators not being controlled will automatically perform basic attacks. Their Battle skills, Combo Skills, and Ultimates must still be manually cast.

Corrosion.lead: Corrosion is an Arts Reaction in Arknights: Endfield.
Corrosion.name: Corrosion
Corrosion.overview:
===Friendly===
Corrosion, when applied to enemies, is a debuff that progressively reduces Resistance. Corrosion lasts for a specified duration and instantly reduces the Resistances against {{Template:Tooltip|all elements|title= All elements|content=Elements include: Physical, Nature, Cryo, Electric, Heat }} of the target by a flat amount and further reduces it over time until a certain minimum. In-game, the Resistance of enemies is rated by letters, starting with 'D' for 0 Resistance, resulting in no reduction for incoming damage; 'C' usually means about 20 Resistance (20% damage reduction or a 0.8 multiplier), and so on.

It is important to note that the Resistance value can be reduced below 0, meaning that Corrosion does work even against enemies that have a Resistance of 0. 

Because of the additive behavior, the effects of Corrosion are more effective on enemies with a higher Resistance:
* Against an enemy with 0 Resistance, reducing it by 24 (to a total of -24 Resistance) results in 24% increased damage taken or a 1.24 multiplier.
* A Heavy Ram has 20 Resistance for incoming Physical Damage, subtracting the 24 points decreases the Resistance value from 20 to -4, turning the 20% reduction into a 4% increase of Physical Damage taken, or in other words, increases the incoming damage multiplier from 0.8 to 1.04, effectively increasing the damage taken by 30% in contrast to the 24% from the first example.

When a Nature Infliction is applied to an enemy with a (//) Non-Nature Infliction, the Arts Infliction that was applied first is consumed instead to trigger Corrosion.
* The debuff lasts for 15s (unless otherwise specified).
* Deals an initial instance of 160% – 400% of ATK (based on the Status Level) as Nature DMG.
* Applies a Resistance Reduction of 3.6 – 7.2 on application that increases by 0.84 – 1.68 each second until it reaches 12 – 24 (based on Status Level).

{| class="wikitable wikitable-mobile"
|-
! Status Level !! Initial Nature DMG !! Initial Resistance Reduction !! Resistance Reduction Increase Over Time !! Max Resistance Reduction
|-
| I || 160% of ATK || 3.6 || 0.84 / second || 12
|-
| II || 240% of ATK || 4.8 || 1.12 / second || 16
|-
| III || 320% of ATK || 6 || 1.4 / second || 20
|-
| IV || 400% of ATK || 7.2 || 1.68 / second || 24
|}

*Arts Intensity increases the amplitude of the Resistance Reduction.
* It is possible to reduce the Resistance of an enemy below zero through Corrosion, causing them to take increased damage.
* Applying Corrosion to a target with an existing Corrosion causes the new Corrosion's Resistance Reduction to be equal to the old Corrosion's Resistance Reduction if it was higher.
** This may cause the new Corrosion to have a Resistance Reduction value that is over its Max Resistance Reduction, in which case the new Corrosion's Resistance Reduction value will be equal to the higher of the two and won't be further increased.
* Some operator skills can also forcibly apply Corrosion without requiring a different Arts Infliction to be consumed (See Arts Reaction for more information).

===Hostile===

As of Dreamscape of Wind and Snow version, there are no enemies capable of applying Corrosion.

Critical Rate.overview:
Damaging hits have a chance to be critical, with the chance being determined by the Critical Rate. The damage of a critical hit is increased by the stat Critical DMG and can trigger effects like the set effect of the MI Security gear set or Artzy Tyrannical's skill.

Each damage instance individually rolls for a crit. For example, it is possible that a single strike hitting multiple enemies lands a critical hit against one enemy, but not a second enemy. Additionally, some Basic Attack Sequences and Skills split up their damage into multiple hits, which also individually roll for a critical hit.

Damage over time effects such as Combustion cannot trigger critical hits. Though it is worth noting that this mechanic is inconsistent throughout the game: Some Skills are described as damage over time effect, despite them being able to crit. For example, Tangtang's Ultimate states "...and deals Cryo DMG over time to enemies..." and is capable of landing critical hits.

=== Enemies ===
Some Enemies are capable of applying Cryo Infliction.
* If the Operator recieves 4 stacks of Cryo Infliction, then Solidification is triggered.

Damage calculation.lead: This article explains the mechanics of damage calculation in Arknights: Endfield.
Damage calculation.name: Damage calculation
Damage calculation.overview:
All numbers are calculated to the exact value, including decimals. When floating damage numbers or values are displayed in-game or in a menu, the value is usually rounded down to the closest integer (e.g. 99.6 is shown as 99).

The formula for most damage is as follows:

 FORMULA: Damage = Attack * Base Multiplier * Multiplier Group FORMULA: * Critical Multiplier * Amp Multiplier FORMULA: * Stagger Multiplier * Finisher Multiplier FORMULA: * Link Multiplier * Weaken Multiplier FORMULA: * Susceptibility Multiplier * Increased DMG Taken Multiplier FORMULA: * DMG Reduction Multiplier * Protection Multiplier FORMULA: * Defense Multiplier * Resistance Multiplier FORMULA: * Multiplicative Multiplier

===Attack===
This is the base value for almost all outgoing damage, and can be seen on the Operator sceen. Percentage increases ("Attack + x%") are only applied to the Base ATK consisting out of the Operator and Weapon ATK. A Special Bonus can be received in certain Protocol Spaces.

 FORMULA: Attack = ((Operator Attack + Weapon Attack) * Percentage Bonuses + Fixed Bonus + Special Bonus ) FORMULA: * Attribute Bonus

with:
 FORMULA: Attribute Bonus = 1 + 0.005 * Main Attribute + 0.002 * Secondary Attribute

===Base Multiplier===
The base multiplier for Basic Attacks and Skills, the values can be seen in-game. For example, Perlica's Battle Skill has a 1.78 DMG Multiplier on Rank 1. The Base Multiplier for other effects such as Crush or Combustion are listed in the section below.

===Multiplier Group===
 FORMULA: Multiplier Group = 1 + Damage Bonuses

This multiplier group sums up many various damage increases that are described as "... DMG Bonus". This includes:
*Damage type specific increases, for example "Physical DMG Bonus"
*Skill type specific increases, for example "Battle DMG Damage Bonus"
*"DMG Bonus vs. Staggered"
*"DMG Bonus"

===Critical Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Critical Multiplier = cases 1 + Critical DMG, & if the hit is critical\\ 1, & if the hit is not critical cases

The base Critical Rate of Operators is 5%, and the Critical DMG is 50%. A critical hit will have "Crit" displayed above its floating damage number. Damage over time effects cannot crit. Though it is worth noting that this mechanic is inconsistent throughout the game: Some Skills are described as damage over time effect, despite them being able to crit.

===Amp Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Amp Multiplier = 1 + Amp Bonuses

Amp can increase the damage dealt. All applicable bonuses are added together. Amp is usually only active for specific damage types. For example, Antal can apply Electric Amp and Heat Amp with his Ultimate.

===Stagger Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Stagger Multiplier = cases 1.3, & if the target is staggered\\ 1, & if the target is not staggered cases

Most enemies have a certain amount of Stagger HP, represented as a bar underneath their healt bar. Dealing Stagger fills the bar. Once the bar is filled, the enemy will be staggered and takes increased damage.

===Finisher Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Finisher Multiplier = cases 1, & if the attack is not a finisher\\ 1, & if the target is an Common Enemy\\ 1.25, & if the target is an Advanced Enemy\\ 1.5, & if the target is an Elite or Alpha Enemy\\ 1.75, & if the target is an Boss Enemy cases

The first basic attack against a staggered enemy becomes a Finisher. This finisher has a special multiplier that is tied to the specific enemy. Currently the values are the same for enemies of the same tier.

===Link Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Link Multiplier = cases 1 + Link Bonus, & if the Skill used a Link buff\\ 1, & if no Link buff is used cases

Link increases the damage dealt by the next Battle Skill or Ultimate cast by the team. Link buffs can stack, but have diminishing returns:
*Link Bonus for Battle Skills: 30/45/60/75%
*Link Bonus for Ultimates: 20/30/40/50%

===Weakness Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Weakness Multiplier = (1 - Weakness Effect)

Weakness decreases the damage dealt. Multiple sources of Weakness stack multiplicately. Currently only Catcher and Camille are capable of applying this effect.

===Susceptibility Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Susceptibility Multiplier = 1 + (Susceptibility Effect * Susceptibility Effect Multiplier)

Susceptibility increases the damage taken. Multiple sources of the same susceptibility such as two different sources of Arts Susceptibility or both Arts Susceptibility and Heat Susceptibility on the same unit stack additively and are classified under Susceptibility Effect.

Effects that use the wording "The effect of that Susceptibility is 1.X times the original" stacks multiplicatively with the summation of Susceptibility Effects and are classified under Susceptibility Effect Multiplier. Currently, the only example is {{Icon|Last Rite icon|text=false}} {{C|Last Rite|g=0}}'s Talent Cryogenic Embrittlement.

===Increased DMG Taken Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Increased DMG Taken Multiplier = 1 + Increased DMG Taken Multiplier

This multiplier describes effects that state "increase DMG Taken" which are not Susceptibility effects. All applicable increases are added together. For example, the effects of Electrification, Breach and the Endministrator's Talent "Realspace Stasis" ("enemies suffer Physical DMG Taken +10%") are in this multiplier group.

===DMG Reduction Multiplier===
 FORMULA: DMG Reduction Multiplier = (1 - DMG Reduction Effects)

This multiplier describes the effect gained from some gear pieces called "Final DMG Reduction" which is different from the damage reduction gained from DEF. This Final DMG Reduction applies to all forms of damage, including Æther DMG. This effect is listed in the Attributes & Stats screen as "[Damage type] DMG Reduction".

===Protection Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Protection Multiplier = 1 - (Protection Effect)

Protect can reduce the damage taken. Only the strongest effect applies. For example, Catcher's Battle Skill grants Protection. While this multiplier is meant to decrease incoming damage, it can actually do the opposite if the Protection value is negative. What can be assumed to be an oversight, a negative Protection value is achievable with Purrchena.

===Defense===
 FORMULA: Defense Multiplier = cases (100)/(DEF + 100), & if DEF is 0 \\ 2-0.99^-DEF, & if DEF is < 0 cases

Defense, or DEF for short, influences the damage taken. All Operators have 0 and all enemies have 100 initial Defense, independent of their level. Defense is mainly increased by equipping Gear, and is otherwise only rarely increased by other sources. Catcher's Potential Bonus Spec Training for example grants him another 20 Defense. Certain effects such as a hostile Combustion ignores the Defense of an Operator.

Equipping four pieces of level 70 gold Gear gives 140 DEF, resulting in a 0.416 multiplier for incoming Damage, or 58.33% DMG Reduction. Enemies having 100 DEF results in a 0.5 multiplier.

Negative Defense values are currently not achievable and remain to be tested once it becomes possible again.

===Resistance Multiplier===
For Operators:

 FORMULA: Physical Resistance = 100 - (100)/(AGI*0.001+1)

 FORMULA: Arts Resistance = 100 - (100)/(INT*0.001+1)

For enemies:

 FORMULA: Resistance Multiplier = (100 - Enemy Resistance + Ignore Resistance + Corrosion Shred)/(100)

This multiplier describes the effect gained from Agility and Intellect, as well as the elemental resistances of enemies. In-game these resistance values are shown as percentage points for Operators and rated with letters for enemies. Starting with 'D' for no resistance, or a 1.0 multiplier, 'C' for some resistance and so on. The accurate multipliers can be seen on the respective enemy pages. Corrosion takes effect in this multiplier. It is worth noting that this multiplier can go above 1.0 and that "ignore Resistance" effects do work even if an enemy has no resistance to speak of.

===Multiplicative Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Multiplicative Multiplier = (1+ Multiplicative Bonus)

This multiplier describes all other bonuses that have a multiplicative effect to each other and to the damage. These bonuses' descriptions are usually indistinguishable from other damage increases as they are marked as "DMG Boost" or "DMG Bonus", although they are far rarer.

*Si is able to deal Fixed DMG, which is not affected by any other multipliers.
**In her specific case, the Fixed DMG depends on the recorded damage dealt to Enemies, which in turn is influenced by the various multipliers. The Fixed DMG dealt here therefore acts more like an independed damage multiplier and avoids being affected by the same multipliers twice.
*Industrial Explosives deal FORMULA: 1250 + Attack * 1.2 Physical DMG, which is affected by all other applicable multipliers such as Defense, Resistance, Physical DMG Bonus and so forth.
*Æthillu take 4% of their maximum HP as damage per tick after reviving. This damage is not affected by any other multiplier and is internally referenced as "LifeDrain".

 FORMULA: Finisher Multiplier = cases 1, & if the attack is not a finisher\\ 1, & if the target is an Common Enemy\\ 1.25, & if the target is an Advanced Enemy\\ 1.5, & if the target is an Elite or Alpha Enemy\\ 1.75, & if the target is an Boss Enemy cases

The first basic attack against a staggered enemy becomes a Finisher. This finisher has a special multiplier that is tied to the specific enemy. Currently the values are the same for enemies of the same tier.

===Link Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Link Multiplier = cases 1 + Link Bonus, & if the Skill used a Link buff\\ 1, & if no Link buff is used cases

Link increases the damage dealt by the next Battle Skill or Ultimate cast by the team. Link buffs can stack, but have diminishing returns:
*Link Bonus for Battle Skills: 30/45/60/75%
*Link Bonus for Ultimates: 20/30/40/50%

===Weakness Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Weakness Multiplier = (1 - Weakness Effect)

Weakness decreases the damage dealt. Multiple sources of Weakness stack multiplicately. Currently only Catcher and Camille are capable of applying this effect.

===Susceptibility Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Susceptibility Multiplier = 1 + (Susceptibility Effect * Susceptibility Effect Multiplier)

Susceptibility increases the damage taken. Multiple sources of the same susceptibility such as two different sources of Arts Susceptibility or both Arts Susceptibility and Heat Susceptibility on the same unit stack additively and are classified under Susceptibility Effect.

Effects that use the wording "The effect of that Susceptibility is 1.X times the original" stacks multiplicatively with the summation of Susceptibility Effects and are classified under Susceptibility Effect Multiplier. Currently, the only example is {{Icon|Last Rite icon|text=false}} {{C|Last Rite|g=0}}'s Talent Cryogenic Embrittlement.

===Increased DMG Taken Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Increased DMG Taken Multiplier = 1 + Increased DMG Taken Multiplier

This multiplier describes effects that state "increase DMG Taken" which are not Susceptibility effects. All applicable increases are added together. For example, the effects of Electrification, Breach and the Endministrator's Talent "Realspace Stasis" ("enemies suffer Physical DMG Taken +10%") are in this multiplier group.

===DMG Reduction Multiplier===
 FORMULA: DMG Reduction Multiplier = (1 - DMG Reduction Effects)

This multiplier describes the effect gained from some gear pieces called "Final DMG Reduction" which is different from the damage reduction gained from DEF. This Final DMG Reduction applies to all forms of damage, including Æther DMG. This effect is listed in the Attributes & Stats screen as "[Damage type] DMG Reduction".

===Protection Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Protection Multiplier = 1 - (Protection Effect)

Protect can reduce the damage taken. Only the strongest effect applies. For example, Catcher's Battle Skill grants Protection. While this multiplier is meant to decrease incoming damage, it can actually do the opposite if the Protection value is negative. What can be assumed to be an oversight, a negative Protection value is achievable with Purrchena.

===Defense===
 FORMULA: Defense Multiplier = cases (100)/(DEF + 100), & if DEF is 0 \\ 2-0.99^-DEF, & if DEF is < 0 cases

Defense, or DEF for short, influences the damage taken. All Operators have 0 and all enemies have 100 initial Defense, independent of their level. Defense is mainly increased by equipping Gear, and is otherwise only rarely increased by other sources. Catcher's Potential Bonus Spec Training for example grants him another 20 Defense. Certain effects such as a hostile Combustion ignores the Defense of an Operator.

Equipping four pieces of level 70 gold Gear gives 140 DEF, resulting in a 0.416 multiplier for incoming Damage, or 58.33% DMG Reduction. Enemies having 100 DEF results in a 0.5 multiplier.

Negative Defense values are currently not achievable and remain to be tested once it becomes possible again.

===Resistance Multiplier===
For Operators:

 FORMULA: Physical Resistance = 100 - (100)/(AGI*0.001+1)

 FORMULA: Arts Resistance = 100 - (100)/(INT*0.001+1)

For enemies:

 FORMULA: Resistance Multiplier = (100 - Enemy Resistance + Ignore Resistance + Corrosion Shred)/(100)

This multiplier describes the effect gained from Agility and Intellect, as well as the elemental resistances of enemies. In-game these resistance values are shown as percentage points for Operators and rated with letters for enemies. Starting with 'D' for no resistance, or a 1.0 multiplier, 'C' for some resistance and so on. The accurate multipliers can be seen on the respective enemy pages. Corrosion takes effect in this multiplier. It is worth noting that this multiplier can go above 1.0 and that "ignore Resistance" effects do work even if an enemy has no resistance to speak of.

===Multiplicative Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Multiplicative Multiplier = (1+ Multiplicative Bonus)

This multiplier describes all other bonuses that have a multiplicative effect to each other and to the damage. These bonuses' descriptions are usually indistinguishable from other damage increases as they are marked as "DMG Boost" or "DMG Bonus", although they are far rarer.

sections.Physical Statuses, Arts Bursts and Arts:
Physical Status, Arts Burst and Arts Reaction are special sources of damage that will be explained in this section.

===Base Multiplier===
* Lift and Knock Down: 120%
* Crush: 150% + 150% per Vulnerable stack
* Breach: 50% + 50% per Vulnerable stack
* Arts Burst: 160% (regardless of the number of Inflictions)
* Arts Reaction: 80% + 80% per infliction stack
* Shatter: 120% + 120% per Status Level
* Combustion DMG Over Time : 12% + 12% per Status Level

In addition to the multipliers listed before, the effects are also increased by two more multipliers:

===Hidden Multiplier===
There is a hidden multiplier that increases the damage from Physical Statuses, Arts Bursts and Arts Reactions. This multiplier is dependent on the level of the Operator. While actually being a value stored for each level, it can be calculated using this formula:

For Physical Status:

 FORMULA: Hidden Multiplier = 1 + (Operator Level - 1)/(392)

For Arts Burst, Arts Reaction and Shatter:

 FORMULA: Hidden Multiplier = 1 + (Operator Level - 1)/(196)

Enemies do not posses this multiplier, as it can be tested in Earthshaking Hazefyre, and therefore do not benefit from this multiplier.

===Arts Intensity Multiplier===
 FORMULA: Arts Intensity Multiplier = 1 + (Arts Intensity)/(100)

Arts Intensity further increases the damage done by the various Physical Statuses, Arts Bursts and Arts Reactions. Each point of Arts Intensity increases the damage done by 1%.

Electrification.overview:
===Friendly===
Electrification, when applied to enemies, is a debuff that increases Arts DMG Taken.

When an Electric Infliction is applied to an enemy with a (//) Non-Electric Infliction, the Arts Infliction that was applied first is consumed to trigger Electrification.
* The debuff lasts for 12 – 30s (based on the Status Level).
* Deals an initial instance of 160% – 400% of ATK (based on the Status Level) as Electric DMG.
* Applies Arts DMG Taken +12% – 24% (based on the Status Level).
{| class="wikitable wikitable-mobile"
|-
! Status Level !! Initial Electric DMG !! Increased Arts DMG Taken !! Duration
|-
| I || 160% of ATK || Arts DMG Taken +12% || 12s
|-
| II || 240% of ATK || Arts DMG Taken +16% || 18s
|-
| III || 320% of ATK || Arts DMG Taken +20% || 24s
|-
| IV || 400% of ATK || Arts DMG Taken +24% || 30s
|}
* Applying Electrification to a target with existing Electrification overrides the previous effect and resets the debuff's duration (unless otherwise specified).
* Some operator skills can also forcibly apply Electrification without requiring a different Arts Infliction to be consumed (see Arts Reaction for more information).

===Hostile===

Some Enemies are capable of applying Electrification.
* The debuff lasts for about 10 seconds.
* Operators are stunned for 1 second upon receiving the debuff, preventing the Operator from taking any action.
* Operators take 20% more Arts Damage for the duration of the debuff.
* Operator also cannot receive any further Electric Inflictions. The Electrification effect is visualized by a darker yellow health bar and the Operator's model glows yellow.

Currently, only the YSTF Captain Blightshade in the Umbral Monument stage Arc of Shadow Flare is capable of applying Electric Inflictions and the resulting Electrification. The stage mechanics dispels all Inflictions from Operators after the enemy inflicts Electric Infliction for the fourth time, and therefore should make it impossible to reach the 4 stacks required for the Electrification, but through the use of Snowshine's Arts Infliction immunity it is sometimes possible to cause a desync, resulting in the hostile Electrification on Operators.

{{Operator page tab}}
Operators are the playable characters in Arknights: Endfield.
Operator.name: Operator
Operator.overview:
Operators have many abilities, ranging from directly fighting the enemy either with melee or long-ranged weaponry, using Originium Arts to attack the enemy with destructive magic, healing other Operators, or providing some form of offensive or defensive support.

Operators can be distinguished not only by their Class, Weapon type, and Element, but also by their unique Skills and Talents.

Many Operators are aligned with Endfield Industries, though some serve as contacts or liaisons for their Faction, while others act as mercenaries or volunteers. This does not affect their accessibility or usage in gameplay.

===Teams===

Operators are assigned to teams, with each one consisting of up to four unique Operators. One Operator can be assigned to multiple different teams.
Players have access to five squads, of which one is actively deployed. Teams can also be renamed.

===Acquisition===
Operators can be obtained through Headhunting. A few selected Operators also join the players' roster during the main story or through sign-in events.

===Attributes===

Operators' Attributes are displayed on the left side of the Character Overview page, below the character name. The icon of the Main Attribute of an Operator is shown in white with a yellow square, while the Secondary Attribute is shown in a grey square. Other Attributes are displayed with a dark grey icon.

Raising an Operator's level, equipping Gear, and increasing the Operator's Potential can provide a bonus to their Attributes.

sections.Overview:
Operators have many abilities, ranging from directly fighting the enemy either with melee or long-ranged weaponry, using Originium Arts to attack the enemy with destructive magic, healing other Operators, or providing some form of offensive or defensive support.

Operators can be distinguished not only by their Class, Weapon type, and Element, but also by their unique Skills and Talents.

Many Operators are aligned with Endfield Industries, though some serve as contacts or liaisons for their Faction, while others act as mercenaries or volunteers. This does not affect their accessibility or usage in gameplay.

===Teams===

Operators are assigned to teams, with each one consisting of up to four unique Operators. One Operator can be assigned to multiple different teams.
Players have access to five squads, of which one is actively deployed. Teams can also be renamed.

===Acquisition===
Operators can be obtained through Headhunting. A few selected Operators also join the players' roster during the main story or through sign-in events.

===Attributes===

Operators' Attributes are displayed on the left side of the Character Overview page, below the character name. The icon of the Main Attribute of an Operator is shown in white with a yellow square, while the Secondary Attribute is shown in a grey square. Other Attributes are displayed with a dark grey icon.

Raising an Operator's level, equipping Gear, and increasing the Operator's Potential can provide a bonus to their Attributes.
sections.Progression:
===Level===

Raising an Operator's level increases their Attributes, as well as their Base ATK and Base HP. Levels can be increased by granting Experience through Operator EXP materials. Operators below level 20 also gain Experience when Enemies are defeated. Leveling an Operator beyond level 10 additionally requires T-Creds. The maximum Level an Operator can reach is 90, but there are several Level caps along the way. Upon reaching a Level cap, the Operator needs to be promoted first, before they can be leveled again. All Operators have the same costs to level up, regardless of their rarity.

It is worth noting that, although higher Levels require an increasing amount of Experience and T-Creds, the amount of Stats gained remains the same. For example, upgrading the Endministrator from level 10 to 11 increases their ATK from 59 to 62, and upgrading them from level 80 to 81 increases their ATK from 287 to 290. In both cases, they gained 3 ATK, but the last-mentioned level-up needs more than 60 times the amount of experience compared to the level-up from 10 to 11. Also, unlike Weapons, any excess EXP gained above a level cap does not get returned and is instead lost.

The Experience amounts provided by different Items are as follows:
* Combat Records used for Operators level 1 - 60
** Elementary Combat Record provide 200 Operator EXP
** Intermediate Combat Record provide 1,000 Operator EXP
** Advanced Combat Record provide 10,000 Operator EXP
* Cognitive Carriers used for Operators level 61 - 90
** Elementary Cognitive Carrier provide 1,000 Operator EXP
** Advanced Cognitive Carrier provide 10,000 Operator EXP

* Level 20: 22,860 EXP and 820 T-Creds
* Level 40: 271,400 EXP and 13,360 T-Creds
* Level 60: 747,110 EXP and 37,260 T-Creds
* Level 80: 1,212,340 EXP and 146,440 T-Creds

In the Talent Nodes section of the Ability Matrix, the player can unlock and upgrade various passive effects displayed as nodes for the Operator. These include an Attribute increase, Talents, Base Skills, Gear nodes, and also their Promotion level. Most of the Nodes have the same unlock costs across all Operators, except for some Talent Nodes, which can have varied costs depending on whether the Talent is already unlocked on E0 and how many ranks the Talent has, and the Endministrator, who does not have any Base Skills and no Trust requirements for the Attribute Increase nodes.

===Potential===
An Operator's Potential can be upgraded to unlock various passive effects, which often include improvements to their Skills and Talents, a flat increase to Attributes, and cost reductions for Ultimates.
Operators have six stages of Potential, starting at 0 and ending at 5, denoted by white lines going counterclockwise that gradually form an inverted pentagram, with a yellow overlay indicating the next level. Operator Potentials can be increased by using Potential Tokens of the respective Operator, raising the Potential by one for each Token used.

Upgrading a 6-star Operator to their full Potential also changes their appearance, usually adding a glow effect to their equipment.

===Cost Summary===
This is the total cost that is required to max out a single Operator, excluding equippable items (such as Weapons, Essences, Gear and their artificing), Talents (because of their differing costs across Operators), and Potentials:
* T-Creds
* Advanced Combat Record or Advanced Combat Record, Intermediate Combat Record, Elementary Combat Record
* Advanced Cognitive Carrier or Advanced Cognitive Carrier, Elementary Cognitive Carrier
* Protoprism, Protohedron
* Kalkodendra, Chrysodendra, Vitrodendra, 84 Valuable Vitrified Plants such as Blighted Jadeleaf or False Aggela
* Pink Bolete, Red Bolete, Ruby Bolete, 8 Fungal Matter such as Bloodcap or Cosmagaric
* 252 Rare Progression Materials (for example D96 Steel Sample 4) 
* Protodisk, Protoset
* Mark of Perseverance

Skill Points.overview:
Skill Points, or SP for short, are used to cast Battle Skills and are shared by all team members. Players can hold up to 300 SP, displayed in the HUD as three segmented bars of 100 SP each. A full bar is indicated with a pulsating yellow, while a partially filled bar appears white. Most Battle Skills consume 100 SP when used, with some consuming 50 or 25 SP instead.

===In Combat===
During combat, SP regenerates naturally at a rate of 8 SP per second. Additional SP can be gained through various actions:
* Hitting an enemy with a Final Strike restores SP based on the controlled Operator, ranging from 15 SP as Fluorite and up to 30 SP as Last Rite.
* A Perfect Dodge recovers approximately 7.5 SP, but pauses the natural regenaration for half a second.
* Performing a Finisher recovers SP based on the enemy.
* Fully destroying Shield Stacks of an enemy restores a small amount of SP.
* Some Skills, notably those of Vanguards, can also recover SP.
* Many other Skills and effects can also return SP.
Returned SP is treated differently from naturally regenerated or recovered SP: it does not trigger SP Recovery-triggered effects and spending returned SP does not grant Ultimate Energy.

Solidification.lead: Solidification is an Arts Reaction in Arknights: Endfield.
Solidification.name: Solidification
Solidification.overview:
Solidification is a debuff applied by Operators and Enemies. Solidification lasts for a duration and prevents the unit from taking action.
===Friendly===
Some Operators are capable of applying Solidification.
* The debuff lasts for 5.75 – 8.75s (based on the Status Level).
* When an operator applies Cryo Infliction to an enemy with a (//) Non-Cryo Infliction, the Arts Infliction that was applied first is consumed to trigger Solidification.
** Deals an initial instance of 160% – 400% of ATK (based on the Status Level) as Base (Unofficial term: Before being increased or decreased by other effects) Cryo DMG.
** Applying Vulnerable or a Physical Status consumes the debuff to trigger Shatter and deal 240% – 600% of ATK (based on the Status Level) as Base (Unofficial term: Before being increased or decreased by other effects) Physical DMG. This is considered as Shatter DMG.

* Some operator skills can also forcibly apply Solidification without requiring a different Arts Infliction to be consumed.
** Forced Solidification does not consume any Arts Inflictions (if any) and applies the reaction as Status Level I (unless otherwise specified).
** Forced Solidification does not trigger the initial instance of Cryo DMG caused by applying multiple Arts Inflictions of different elements.

===Hostile===

Some Enemies are capable of applying Solidification.
* When an Operator reaches 4 stacks of Cryo Infliction, all existing Cryo Infliction stacks are removed to trigger Solidification.
** Prevents the Operator from taking action over the debuff duration. This includes any movement or skill actions. If the controlled Operator is solidifed, the player will be also unable to switch Operators.
* The debuff lasts 3.5s (unless otherwise specified). {{Needs Verification}}.
* While under the effects of Solidification, the debuffed operator cannot be inflicted by further Cryo Inflictions.

Stagger.lead: Stagger is a combat mechanic in Arknights: Endfield.
Stagger.name: Stagger

sections.Description:
Most Enemies have a Stagger meter, which can be filled by various actions such as:
*Final Strikes,
*Battle Skills, Combo Skills or Ultimates,
*Physical Status

When the Stagger meter is full, Enemies will enter the Staggered state; When Staggered, Enemies are immobile for a while and take 30% increased damage. Additionally, the first Basic Attack from the currently controlled Operator becomes a Finisher, dealing increased damage and restoring SP. While staggered, Enemies can't receive more stagger. After a certain amount of time passed the Enemy will recover from its staggered state.

Some Enemies, usually powerfull ones such categorized as Alpha or Boss, also have Stagger Nodes on their Stagger meter. When enough Stagger is build up to reach a Stagger Node, the Enemy will be interrupted and stumbles for a short time.

Certain Weapons and Gear can increase the wearer's damage against Staggered Enemies or the amount of Stagger applied.

{{Icon|Susceptibility icon|text=false|nolink=true}} Susceptibility is a category of debuffs inflicted to enemies in Arknights: Endfield.

As of October 2026, there are currently no operators who directly apply Susceptibility, although it appears as an icon through enemies affected by {{Icon|Ardelia icon|Ardelia's}} Battle Skill Dolly Rush which applies both Physical Susceptibility and Arts Susceptibility. Applying both types of Susceptibility through different operators does not show the icon.

When enemies are inflicted with a type of Susceptibility, they temporarily take more damage for a set duration based on the type inflicted and the Element of the incoming damage type. The number represents the degree of increase.

An enemy that is considered Arts Susceptible is also considered Susceptible to all Arts Elements. For example, while {{Icon|Avywenna icon|Avywenna's}} {{Icon|Potential 5|Carrot and Sharp Stick}} only explicitly states that it is triggered from enemies that are Electric Susceptible, applying Arts Susceptibility to the target also triggers this Potential.

Multiple sources of Susceptibility stack additively to form the Susceptibility Multiplier for that damage instance. The resulting Susceptibility Mulitplier then stacks multiplicatively with other damage multipliers to get the final value. For more information on calculating damage, see Damage calculation.

Ultimate Energy.lead: Ultimate Energy is a combat resource in Arknights: Endfield.
Ultimate Energy.name: Ultimate Energy
Ultimate Energy.overview:
Ultimate Energy is used to cast Ultimates. Each Operator stores Ultimate Energy independently, up to a maximum value that varies between different Operators. Once this maximum is reached, the Operator's Ultimate can be cast, consuming all Ultimate Energy and placing the Ultimate on a short cooldown. The amount of Ultimate Energy stored is displayed next to the Operator’s Battle Skill as a hollow circular gauge (or a curved bar on certain devices), which fills proportionally to the stored charge.

===Gaining Ultimate Energy===
There are two primary sources of Ultimate Energy:
* While in combat, casting Battle Skills grants Ultimate Energy to everyone in the team at a ratio of 6.5 per 100 non-returned SP spent. Many offensive Battle Skills require at least one enemy hit to generate Ultimate Energy.
* Most Combo Skills grant 10 Ultimate Energy to the caster. Many offensive Combo Skills require at least one enemy hit to generate Ultimate Energy. Some skills distribute the Ultimate Energy gained across individual hits, for example Akekuri's Flash and Dash grants 5 Ultimate Energy per sequence hit.

Some Operators deviate from this standard:
* Arclight gains only 5 Ultimate Energy from her Combo Skill
* Avywenna does not get any Ultimate Energy directly from her Combo Skill. Instead, her Talent provides Ultimate Energy.
* Last Rite has a special trait making her gain Ultimate Energy only from her Battle and Combo Skill. Other sources, including consumables, do not grant her Ultimate Energy.
* Rossi gains an additional 10 Ultimate Energy from the second sequence of her Battle Skill, and both sequences of her Combo Skill grant 10 Ultimate Energy.
* Liino gains 20 Ultimate Energy from her Combo Skill

A few Operators have Talents or Potentials that allow them to gain extra Ultimate Energy, for example Alesh's Talent "Flash-frozen for Freshness" or Estella's Potential "Survival is a Win".

Ultimates that enhance Operators, for example Laevatain's Twilight, can not gain Ultimate Energy while the enchancement is active.

The stat "Ultimate Gain Efficiency" can increase the amount of Ultimate Energy gained.

===Ultimate Costs===
Ultimate costs typically range between 70 and 120 Ultimate Energy. However, the six-star Strikers Laevatain, Last Rite, and Yvonne have significantly higher costs, exceeding 200. This is accompanied by significant more Ultimate Energy gained through their skills.

The cost of Ultimates can be reduced through activating certain Potentials.

Weapon.overview:
Each Operator has a predefined Weapon type that they can use, all Weapons of other different types cannot be equipped. While a Weapon can only be equipped by one Operator at a time, regardless of whether they are on the active team or not, Weapons can be freely swapped around between different Operators and the Inventory.

A significant proportion of an Operator's Base ATK comes from their equipped Weapon, with higher rarity Weapons generally providing a higher Base ATK than lower rarity ones. Weapons also have three Skills: The first is a generic Attribute buff, and the second is an buff for Secondardy Stats, such as HP, Crit Rate or a specific damage type. The third Skill is unique to each Weapon and usually grants a positive effect under certain conditions such as restoring HP or giving a ATK buff to the entire team after applying Electrification. Note that 3★ Weapons do not have a third Skill, and that the Attribute and Secondary Stats Skills on lower rarity Weapons are generally weaker than those found on 6★ Weapons, marked by a [S] on 4★ Weapons and a [M] for 5★ Weapons.

Equipping a Weapon which Skills align with those of the Operator is crucial for achieving better combat results. For instance, a Weapon that increases Strength and Heat damage should, in most cases, only be used by Operators who have Strength as their Main or Secondary Attribute and can actually deal Heat damage.

Currently, there are five Weapon types:

*Sword: The typical melee weapon, mostly used by Guards.
*Great Sword: More heavier weapon with a slower attack speed, but deals more Stagger; Used by most Defender Operators.
*Polearm: Lighter weapon for Operators that rely on skills.
*Handcannon: One of the ranged weapons that is used by Operators relying on Arts Reactions.
*Arts Unit: A spherical, drone-looking ranged weapon mostly used by Casters and Supports.

===Obtaining===
While most of the Weapons can only be obtained via Arsenal Exchange, 3★ Weapons are only obtained when recruiting a new Operator, all 4★ Weapons can be found during exploration by opening Crates, and a few selected 5★ Weapons can be purchased from Stock Redistribution. Special Weapon Supply items allow the player to choose a Weapon from a selection. Some Weapons such as Farsight are also only given out as Event rewards.

sections.Progression:
===Level===
Raising a Weapon's level significantly increases its Attack stat which can be done by giving it Experience using Weapon Progression Materials and/or other Weapons. Upgrading beyond level 10 also requires T-Creds. The maximum level a Weapon can reach is 90, but there are several level caps along the way. Upon reaching a level cap, the Weapon needs to be tuned first, before it can be leveled again. All weapons have the same costs to level up, regardless of their rarity.

It is worth noting that, although higher levels require an increasing amount of Experience and T-Creds, the amount of Attack Power gained remains the same. For example, upgrading a Mountain Bearer from level 10 to 11 increases its ATK from 96 to 101 and upgrading it from level 79 to 80 increases its ATK from 444 to 449. In both cases it gained 5 ATK, but the last mentioned level up needs more than 300 times the amount of Experience compared to the level up from 10 to 11.

The Experience amounts provided by different Items and Weapons are as follows:
* Items
** Arms Inspector provide 200 Weapon EXP
** Arms INSP Kit provide 1,000 Weapon EXP
** Arms INSP Set provide 10,000 Weapon EXP
* Weapons
** Weapons provide 500 Weapon EXP
** Weapons provide 1,500 Weapon EXP
** Weapons provide 10,000 Weapon EXP
** Weapons provide 30,000 Weapon EXP

Weapons used as material will grant its base EXP (based on rarity) and any invested EXP into the upgrading Weapon, and refund any invested T-Creds (but not Tuning Materials). A Weapon with increased Potential will not provide more EXP than one of the same level but with less Potential.
Also, any excess EXP above a Level cap gets partially returned in increments of 200 EXP. For example, upgrading a Weapon from level 19 to 20 using Arms INSP Set would provide 10,000 EXP out of the 1,900 needed, returning Arms INSP Kit worth 8000 EXP.

These are the cumulative costs to upgrade a Weapon to a specific level from level 1:
* Level 20: 8,890 EXP and 640 T-Creds
* Level 40: 105,540 EXP and 10,400 T-Creds
* Level 60: 290,540 EXP and 29,010 T-Creds
* Level 80: 1,203,710 EXP and 123,850 T-Creds
* Level 90: 2,524,080 EXP and 341,390 T-Creds

===Tuning===

All Weapons start at Tuning Stage 0 with an initial level cap of 20. Once a Weapon has reached its level cap, it can be tuned using Tuning Materials to raise the level cap and also improve the Weapon's Skills.

Each Tuning Stage increases the upper rank limits of a Weapon's first and second Skill by 1. Additionally, at T1 and T3, the first Skill's base rank and upper rank limit are increased by an extra level, while at T2 and T4, the same applies to the second Skill. In total, tuning a Weapon to T4 increases both its first and second skills by 2 ranks each and raises their rank limits by 6.
For 3★ Weapons, only the first Skill is upgraded.

===Potential===

A Weapon's Potential can be upgraded to increase the base and upper rank limit of its third Skill. For 3★ weapons, the second Skill is improved instead.
Weapons have six stages of Potential, starting at 0 and ending at 5, denoted by white lines going counterclockwise that gradually form an inverted pentagram, with a yellow overlay indicating the next level. Weapon Potentials can be increased by using duplicates of the same Weapon, raising the Potential by one for each Weapon used. Using a Weapon which Potential has already been increased to upgrade another Weapon will transfer the increased Potential to the upgraded Weapon. A Protocolized Weapon Pattern can also be used for certain Weapons to increase their Potential.

Each Potential upgrade increases the Weapon's last Skill base rank and maximum rank by one. In total, upgrading a Weapon's Potential to maximum increases its last Skill by 5 ranks and raises that skill's rank limit from 4 to 9.

Upgrading a 6-star Weapon to its full Potential also changes its appearance.

===Essence===

Defeated Enemies may drop reactive substances called Essences. These items can be infused into a Weapon to enhance its Weapon Skills.

Each Essence carries several potential Weapon Skill upgrades. Infusing a Weapon with a Essence will increase the level of the Weapon Skills that match the ones from the Essence. Higher rarity Essences usually provide higher leveled Weapon Skills than lower rarity ones. Before infusion, players can preview the effects the Essence will grant.

If the infused Essence gives more skill levels than the weapon skill can currently allow due to the weapon not being fully Tuned, then the extra levels will be ignored.

An Essence can only be attached to one Weapon at a time. However, it can be unequipped and freely transferred to another Weapon at any point.

Equipping a Weapon with an Essence that matches all its Weapon Skills also changes its appearance, by adding a small animated glowing part. This does not apply to 3★ weapons. 

A Flawless Essence, that perfectly matches all skills of a weapon is colloquially referred to as a "perfect Essence".
